d: User can turn the unit on or off via the App anytime, anywhere with a network connection.
Select the desired stored water temperature (typically 40°C–75°C depending on capacity and model).
The App calculates and displays the percentage/liters of hot water still available based on tank capacity and current temperature (e.g. a 30L tank at ~60% remaining).
Choose between Fast mode (maximum power, quick heating) and Eco mode (lower power, slower heating but less electricity used).
Shows the actual temperature of water flowing from the shower/sink tap, which may differ from tank temperature due to pipe mixing.
Set the time hot water is needed (e.g. 6:30 AM); the unit calculates the required duration and starts heating in advance — no need to manually turn on and wait.
Maintains water at a lower, energy-saving temperature when there's no scheduled use, raising it before the set time instead of keeping it hot continuously all day.
Set different heating schedules for each day (e.g. later wake-up on weekends).
When enabled, the unit lowers temperature to a minimum maintenance level (preventing scale/bacteria buildup) to maximize savings while unused, automatically restoring settings once turned off.
Automatically shifts the heating schedule to off-peak hours based on the regional electricity tariff the user enters, saving on cost.

g: Safety — Specific to Storage Tank Units
d: Tracks the lifespan of the corrosion- and shock-protection magnesium anode inside the tank, reminding replacement periodically (typically every 12–24 months depending on water quality).

g: Safety — Specific to Storage Tank Units
d: Detects when tank pressure exceeds the safe threshold, warns of risk, and reminds to check the safety valve/check valve.

g: Safety — Specific to Storage Tank Units
d: Logs and notifies each time the safety relief valve self-discharges to reduce pressure, helping detect early if it discharges unusually often (an abnormal sign).

g: Safety — Specific to Storage Tank Units
d: If equipped with a leak sensor, alerts immediately upon detecting water leaking at the tank base or connecting pipes.

g: Safety — Specific to Storage Tank Units
d: Locks physical controls on the unit body; can only be controlled via the password-protected App.
Reports a specific error code when the in-tank temperature sensor fails or loses signal.
Automatically shuts off and alerts if tank temperature exceeds the maximum safe threshold, suspecting the thermal relay is stuck in the on position.
Stores every past error with timestamp for quick reference when contacting warranty support.
Aggregated chart of power consumption by day, week, and month, compared across periods.
Compares keep-warm electricity loss between winter and summer, suggesting seasonal temperature adjustments.
Compares current consumption with the historical average, alerting on a sudden spike — possibly due to heavy scale buildup or heat loss.
Pair the unit with the home WiFi network via the App for remote control.
Assign a memorable name and room to each unit, shown clearly in the device list.
Turn on/off and adjust temperature by voice command via Google Assistant / Amazon Alexa.
Group multiple units (e.g. 1st floor, 2nd floor) to turn on/off or schedule them together with one action.
Invite household members to control the unit together via a secondary account; access can be revoked anytime.
Counts days of use and reminds the user to flush mineral buildup from the tank, especially with hard water sources.
Send a technical support request (anode replacement, valve check, tank flush) directly from the App, choosing a convenient date and time.
Send the activity log and error codes directly to the Livotec support team for remote diagnosis.
Update the unit's control software over WiFi, no need to bring it to a service center.
An electric shutoff valve automatically closes the water supply when a leak is detected, limiting maximum water loss before the user can react. (Ref: Rheem LeakGuard, AO Smith LeakShield)
Analyzes current draw and heating duration to estimate wear on the heating element, alerting early before it fails outright — avoiding a sudden loss of hot water. (Ref: Rheem EcoNet)

Quickly switch between modes: Maximum Energy Saver, High Demand (multiple simultaneous users), Electric-Only, and Away — each mode automatically reconfigures temperature and power accordingly. (Ref: Rheem ProTerra Hybrid)

A special internal flow mechanism flushes mineral scale away instead of letting it settle at the bottom, extending lifespan and maintaining heating efficiency longer between flushes. (Ref: Rheem EverKleen)
The App learns the household's hot water usage pattern by day of week to heat exactly when needed, reducing standby keep-warm loss when no one is using it. (Ref: Aquanta)
Automatically switches to minimum keep-warm mode when all household members leave the configured home radius, restoring normal temperature when someone returns nearby. (Ref: Rheem EcoNet)
When the utility offers a demand-response program, the App voluntarily adjusts keep-warm power during peak hours to earn electricity price incentives. (Ref: Rheem EcoNet, CTA-2045 standard)

Links with the Matter standard, Apple HomeKit, and SmartThings to create cross-device automation scenes at home.
